Question: Where can I find help with my crossdressing?
Answer: Question answered: Where can I find help with my crossdressing? The best type of help you can get is from a woman friend, or from a stylist who’s a woman. Picture yourself at home staring into your closet. If you don’t already have a collection of women’s clothing, then it’s time to get to work! I would start by considering who your women friends are. Are you close enough to any of them to trust them with your crossdressing lifestyle? If the answer is yes, then meet with them privately and come up with a weekly day and time to meet privately — preferably at your home or apartment, but if she prefers to meet at her place, better yet. Another option — one that I actually recommend the most of all — would be to place an advertisement on craigslist in the “Miscellaneous Job Offers” section. It might be under “Gigs” or “Temp Jobs” depending on where you live. Write something interesting. Try this as a headline: “I’m looking for someone to help me get in touch with my feminine side—quite literally”. Then write about 100 words, if not more, describing yourself. Tell the readers that you’re new at crossdressing and would like to meet with a stylist on a weekly basis. You can also ask for models to help you, or for women who have experience with crossdressing men. A very long time ago, that’s exactly what I did and within 48 hours, nearly 50 women applied for the job. I ended up hiring a former model and we worked together for six hours a week for close to a year. Those are some of the fondest memories I have.

Having reviewed nearly five thousand photos of each of these garments, I haven’t be able to find anything wrong with either one of them. Of course, wearing a crop top in the dead of winter wouldn’t make much sense since your stomach would be exposed to wind, rain, sleet and snow. And wearing a hoodie on a trip to Antarctica would also be a problem since the temperatures there would require something much more substantial — thermal underwear, three layers of shirts, a jacket, coat, hat, gloves and boots. So here’s the takeaway from your question: When crop tops and hoodies are worn under the right weather conditions, absolutely nothing is wrong with them.
